requirements.requirement: Add at least 512 MB of disk-backed swap on node1, make it active, and prefer it over any existing swap.
requirements.summary: A 536,870,912-byte swap file is active at priority 100. Its usable swap capacity exceeds 512 MB, it is root-owned with mode 0600, and no other active swap exists.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the added swap is active at boot.
requirements.summary: The single fstab entry successfully reactivated the swap during a bounded swapoff/swapon test. A subsequent reboot changed the boot identity, after which the swap was automatically active at priority 100 and the system had recovered normally.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 16.04 and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic were unchanged from baseline through the post-reboot state. The standard platform-provided swap tools worked successfully, including across reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The swap is sufficiently large, active and persistent, priority-configured, secure, and verified after a real reboot. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities, with recovered system, SSH, swap, and platform state.
limitations: One post-restart assertion command exited nonzero because its usable-KiB threshold was four KiB above the initialized swap's reported capacity. The later corrected final verification passed and directly showed an exact 512 MiB backing file with more than 512 decimal MB active swap, so this does not undermine the outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and configuring /swapfile, activating it, the bounded swapoff/swapon persistence test, and rebooting all directly supported task outcomes or the mandatory restart protocol. The initial unprivileged creation attempt changed no state, as the target remained absent. The scheduled-reboot log was operationally related and left no observed residue after reboot. Final snapshots show no failed services, package damage, unsafe socket exposure, or abnormal temporary-file residue.
